terra.problem: The passage calls them a flock; it does not say they are sheep.
The passage does not say that nothing about the ground changed except who was standing there. It places Moses on the ground and God speaking from the bush, not God standing on the ground.
The passage says Moses hid his face because he was afraid to look at God; it does not prescribe this as the right reaction to hearing God speak.
The passage says Moses led Jethro's flock to Horeb, but it does not identify the flock as sheep or say he came to the mountain for sheep.
The drawer joke makes the eternal remembrance of God's name its setup.
God says the elders will listen, but the passage does not say He has already seen how the meeting goes.
The passage says the king will not let them go unless a mighty hand compels him. It does not specify the outcome of the first request.
The explanation describes the people walking out with their hands full as something that happens here. God is telling Moses what will happen when they leave.
Goliath is introduced without saying who he is.
God promises to help Moses speak, but the passage does not describe Him going with Moses into a room.
The passage promises help and teaching; it does not say Moses will not gain a new ability.
The passage says Aaron is on his way and will be glad to see Moses. It does not say Moses is walking toward him or that Moses will be happy at the meeting.
God says Aaron will be glad when he sees Moses. The explanation presents that meeting and gladness as already happening.
